You are an independent classifier in a blinded experiment about a book of
biblical symbolism. The consensus responses below were produced without access
to the book. Compare them with the book's entry.

TERM
Rock

BLIND CONSENSUS RESPONSES
RESPONSE A
{
  "primary_meaning": "In mainstream Christian teaching, 'rock' primarily symbolizes God (and, in Christian typology, Christ) as an unshakable foundation, refuge, and source of salvation — connoting stability, permanence, protection, and trustworthiness. The New Testament extends this explicitly to Christ, both as the spiritual rock that accompanied Israel (1 Cor 10:4) and as the sure foundation on which faith and the church are built.",

    "Deuteronomy 32:4 (\"He is the Rock, his works are perfect\")",

    "Psalm 95:1 (\"the rock of our salvation\")",

    "Isaiah 26:4 (\"the LORD... is an everlasting rock\")",
    "1 Corinthians 10:4 (\"that rock was Christ\", referencing Exodus 17:6 and Numbers 20:8-11)",
    "Matthew 7:24-25 (the wise man builds his house on the rock)",
    "1 Peter 2:4-8 and Isaiah 28:16 (Christ as cornerstone/foundation stone)",
    "Matthew 16:18 (\"on this rock I will build my church\")"
  ],

      ],

        "1 Peter 2:7-8",

    {
      "meaning": "The struck rock as a type of Christ's atoning death and the source of living water / the Spirit: the rock struck at Horeb prefiguring Christ smitten so that grace flows out.",

        "Jeremiah 23:29"
      ],
      "prominence": "minority"

  "has_settled_consensus": true,
  "confidence": "high",
  "notes": "The core symbolism — God/Christ as rock of refuge, salvation, and foundation — is among the most stable and widely recognized symbols in Christian interpretation, attested from the Hebrew Bible through the New Testament and across patristic, Catholic, Orthodox, and Protestant traditions. The one genuinely contested locus is Matthew 16:18, where the referent of 'this rock' (Peter, Peter's confession, or Christ) divides Catholic and Protestant exegesis; this is a dispute about referent, not about the symbol's basic force (foundation/stability). The 'stumbling stone' and 'struck rock' motifs are complementary rather than competing meanings."
}

However, the symbol is context-dependent, and there is no settled cross-traditional consensus on the specific referent of “this rock” in Matthew 16:18; Peter, Peter’s confession, and Christ are all established readings."

BOOK ENTRY
The covenant — the Rock that followed Israel “was Christ,” the covenant in person; the stone the builders refused, made the cornerstone.

BOOK'S COMMON-VIEW NOTE, IF PRESENT
(none)

SCRIPTURE REFERENCES PRINTED WITH THE ENTRY
(Deut 32:4; Isa 42:6; 1 Cor 10:4; Ps 118:22) · see Mountain, ch. 39

AVAILABLE KJV EXCERPTS
Deuteronomy 32:4 — He is the Rock, his work is perfect: for all his ways are judgment: a God of truth and without iniquity, just and right is he.
Isaiah 42:6 — I the LORD have called thee in righteousness, and will hold thine hand, and will keep thee, and give thee for a covenant of the people, for a light of the Gentiles;
1 Corinthians 10:4 — And did all drink the same spiritual drink: for they drank of that spiritual Rock that followed them: and that Rock was Christ.
Psalms 118:22 — The stone which the builders refused is become the head stone of the corner.

CLASSIFY THE RELATIONSHIP

First reduce both readings to their minimum core identifications. Do not let
extra detail create an artificial disagreement.

- MATCH: the core identifications are equivalent. Differences are merely
  wording or immaterial detail.
- REFINED: the book preserves the consensus's general referent or category but
  materially changes its extension, boundary, conditions, or precision. A
  narrowing may reject some cases the broader consensus admits; a broadening
  may admit cases it excludes. This is real disagreement at the boundary, but
  not replacement of the central referent.
- DIVERGENT: the cores materially contradict. Both claims cannot be true of the
  same referent in the same context and sense; accepting the book requires
  rejecting or replacing the consensus identification. A source and its
  product remain different referents when the book explicitly denies their
  identity, even if they are causally related.
- NOVEL: no recognizable consensus or listed alternative covers the book's
  core identification. Novelty is absence from consensus, not contradiction.

Use `core_relation` to expose the relationship at the center and
`extension_relation` to expose disagreement over the cases covered. A REFINED
verdict must state what cases the book adds, excludes, or reclassifies. A
DIVERGENT verdict must identify a replaced referent or material contradiction,
not merely a narrower boundary.

Treat the two axes independently. A core-divergent reading may still retain
some cases covered by the consensus while rejecting its central identification;
therefore DIVERGENT does not require disjoint extensions. Conversely, a
narrowed extension is REFINED only when the consensus's central referent or
category remains intact.

Also judge whether the citations printed with the glossary entry alone provide
strong, partial, or insufficient support. Do not yet decide whether a divergent
full chapter is persuasive; that is a separate stage.
